answer: A reputation terrace makes fake identities expensive: every new agent starts at the jetty, the lowest tier, where it can only take tiny, supervised jobs. Verified honest work over time lets it climb to higher terraces with bigger jobs and pay, while one proven fraud drops it back down and forfeits its staked bond. An attacker must therefore fund a slow spiral of real, costly work for each clone before any clone earns trust, so cloning a hundred identities costs a hundred times the effort and still yields no shortcut to high-value work.
